phil-meta-01-c1.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2020). Aristotle's Metaphysics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-meta-01-c1.quote: These causes and principles are clearly the subject matter of what he calls ‘first philosophy’.
phil-meta-01-c1.claim: Aristotle himself called the subject first philosophy, the study of being as such, prior to all the special sciences.

phil-meta-01-c2.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2022). Aristotle's Categories. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-meta-01-c2.quote: Instead, he thinks that there are ten: (1) substance; (2) quantity; (3) quality; (4) relatives; (5) somewhere;
phil-meta-01-c2.claim: He sorted how things can be into ten categories: substance, quantity, quality, relation, place, time, position, state, action, and passion.

phil-meta-01-c3.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2022). Jean-Paul Sartre. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-meta-01-c3.quote: Rather, existence precedes essence, as he famously remarks in both Being and Nothingness and Existentialism is a Humanism.
phil-meta-01-c3.claim: Sartre's 'existence precedes essence' claims humans have no fixed essence and that we create ourselves through choices.

phil-meta-04-c1.text: Vihvelin, Kadri (2003). Arguments for Incompatibilism. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-meta-04-c1.quote: If determinism is true, then our acts are the consequence of laws of nature and events in the remote past.
phil-meta-04-c1.claim: The Consequence Argument (van Inwagen): the consequences of laws of nature and past events are not up to us; our actions are consequences of laws and past events;

phil-meta-05-c1.text: Menzies, Peter, Beebee, Helen (2001). Counterfactual Theories of Causation. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-meta-05-c1.quote: The basic idea of counterfactual theories of causation is that the meaning of causal claims can be explained in terms of counterfactual conditionals of the form “If event c had not occurred, event e would not have occurred”.
phil-meta-05-c1.claim: There is no observable 'necessary connection.' Counterfactual analysis (Lewis): C causes E iff if C hadn't occurred, E wouldn't have.
